2608.07250.title: Artificial Intelligence Can Match Domain Experts in Evidence Extraction and Critical Appraisal of Microbial Oncogenesis Research Publications
2608.07250.paper_summary: Confirmed oncogenic microbes contribute significantly to cancer burden. Identifying novel microbial oncogenicity could yield strategies that will reduce disease burdens. However, relevant evidence is dispersed and infeasible for humans to comprehensively synthesize. LLMs may enable scalable, expert-level systematic evidence synthesis to identify microbe-cancer pairs; however, such capabilities have not yet been demonstrated. Domain experts were recruited to create a dataset to benchmark LLM performance (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, GPT-5, GPT-5 Nano) on 24 research papers using MMTV-LV and breast cancer as a case study. We devised a structured template for evidence extraction and appraisal, consisting of MCQ, Likert-scale, multi-select, and free-text question types (77 items across 24 papers). Agreement between (1) experts and (2) experts and each LLM was determined per question instance using novel metrics. LLMs were assessed by comparing inter-expert and expert-LLM agreement distributions to determine whether LLMs behaved as additional experts by increasing or maintaining inter-expert agreement. Free-text responses were further evaluated qualitatively. Across all question types, LLM responses aligned closely with experts, with GPT-5 and GPT-5 Nano achieving score distributions indistinguishable from experts. Gemini models behaved similarly but were significantly more lenient in applying microbial oncogenesis criteria. Hallucinations were rare. Methodological appraisal and identification of contradictions within full-texts were the most persistent LLM vulnerabilities. GPT-5 and GPT-5 Nano were indistinguishable from experts on structured domain research paper evaluation tasks. This supports use of LLMs for automated systematic evidence synthesis. However, methodological appraisal tasks and contradiction identification in full-texts remain weaknesses requiring strengthening.
2608.07250.paper_summary_zh: 確認的腫瘤微生物對癌症負擔有顯著貢獻。識別新型微生物腫瘤性可能會產生減少疾病負擔的策略。然而，相關證據分散，對人類來說無法全面綜合。LLMs 可能使可擴展的專家級系統證據綜合成為可能，以識別微生物-癌症配對；然而，這種能力尚未得到證明。招募了領域專家來創建一個數據集，以基準 LLM 在 24 篇研究論文上的表現（Gemini 2.5 Pro、Gemini 2.5 Flash、GPT-5、GPT-5 Nano），使用 MMTV-LV 和乳腺癌作為案例研究。我們設計了一個結構化模板，用於證據提取和評估，包含 MCQ、李克特量表、多選和自由文本問題類型（24 篇論文中的 77 項）。根據每個問題實例使用新指標確定（1）專家之間和（2）專家與每個 LLM 之間的協議。通過比較專家之間和專家-LLM 協議分佈來評估 LLM，以確定 LLM 是否通過增加或維持專家之間的協議而表現得像額外的專家。自由文本回應進一步進行了質性評估。在所有問題類型中，LLM 的回應與專家密切一致，GPT-5 和 GPT-5 Nano 的得分分佈與專家無法區分。Gemini 模型的表現相似，但在應用微生物腫瘤生成標準方面顯著更寬鬆。幻覺很少見。方法論評估和在全文中識別矛盾是 LLM 最持久的脆弱性。GPT-5 和 GPT-5 Nano 在結構化領域研究論文評估任務中與專家無法區分。這支持了使用 LLM 進行自動化系統證據綜合的可行性。然而，方法論評估任務和在全文中識別矛盾仍然是需要加強的弱點。
